sentence: This project studies how transcription factor activities in Mycobacterium tuberculosis control how well drugs work against it.
This project studies how plants regenerate damaged body parts and which core cellular properties allow it.
This project studies the molecular and cellular mechanisms of noxious cold perception, which can go wrong and lead to neuropathic pain.
This project studies how the motor protein myosin-X helps form finger-like cellular protrusions called filopodia and takes part in cell division.
This project provides investigators with techniques and assays to study adipose tissue and its cell types in mouse and human samples.
This project tests how immunotherapy approaches change the tumor microenvironment of pancreatic adenocarcinoma, using clinical specimens and pre-clinical work.
This project builds computational tools that compare genetic and epigenetic information between animal models and humans, using machine learning models.
This project provides biostatistics and bioinformatics support for clinical and translational research on digestive and liver diseases.
This project engineers the membrane of extracellular vesicles to present specific ligands that restore cellular function after tissue damage due to inflammation.
This project tests whether a tumor's mutational status decides how well radiation therapy enhances responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
This project develops allele specific knockdown as a therapy for a dominantly inherited myopathy that has no treatments.
This project develops imaging technologies that let diffusion MRI show smaller brain microstructural features than it can now.
This project develops instrumentation and protocols for treating inoperable liver cancers with ultrashort electrical pulses, and tests them in a large animal model.
This project tests whether temporal response function modeling is a reliable and valid tool for measuring auditory comprehension in stroke-induced aphasia.
This project combines physical therapy and bioengineering to develop rehabilitation assessments and interventions for chronic diseases.
This project tries to close knowledge gaps about the diagnosis, outcomes and treatment of rheumatic diseases.
This project studies how a kinase limits self-renewal and survival of leukemia stem cells in chronic myeloid leukemia, and looks for drugs that stabilize it.
This project studies genetic and environmental risk factors for clonal hematopoiesis and its role as a risk factor for aging-related chronic diseases including heart failure.
This project uses a system that triggers proteolysis of selected factors to study how Aspergillus fumigatus controls virulence.
This project studies how bacteria in the human aerodigestive tract change their secondary metabolism in response to invading pathogens, and looks for antibiotics they make.
